title: Infographic. Running myth: switching to a non-rearfoot strike reduces injury risk and improves running economy
claims: The infographic states that transitioning to a non-rearfoot strike pattern to reduce injury risk or improve running economy is not supported by evidence.
While knee loads are reduced with forefoot striking, loads to the calf, ankle and foot increase, which may raise injury risk in those areas during transition.
The authors note that retrospective evidence links rearfoot striking with greater injury risk, but that no prospective evidence supports one pattern increasing or decreasing future injury risk.
No difference in running economy was found between habitual rearfoot and habitual non-rearfoot strike runners.
The overwhelming majority of recreational shod distance runners use a rearfoot strike pattern.
